text:
jamie: heads up, westus2 GPU pool telemetry dropped at 02:22 UTC, provisioning backlog started to climb and burst-shed kicked in :rotating_light:
jamie: I'm seeing all node-exporter and nvml exporters stop emitting for the gpu-tenant namespace (metrics count -> 0)
sarah: thanks — are logs present on the nodes? can we still ssh?
miguel: nodes are up, kubelet healthy, but egress to our metrics cluster is intermittently failing. getting TLS handshake errors in exporter logs
leah: @miguel can you paste the exporter error?
miguel: ```
2026-03-18T02:21:58Z exporter.go:142] scrape failed: Post \"https://metrics-collector.redwood.internal/api/v1/write\": dial tcp 10.4.5.6:443: i/o timeout
```
max: noticed similar pattern in ap-logs: agent tried to rotate certs earlier, firewall rule 203 got patched around 02:20 during a maintenance window
jamie: wtf — westus2 maintenance should have been a no-op. who deployed that firewall change?
leah: deploy-bot shows a manual change by infra-ops at 02:18 with description "temporary rule for vendor"
sarah: OK probable cause. immediate mitigation: route metrics egress over fallback NAT gateway and restart daemonset to re-establish connections
miguel: doing: `kubectl -n gpu-tenant rollout restart ds/gpu-exporter` then patching egress route to nat-backup
jamie: heads-up on cost — backup NAT has expensive cross-region path if it stays long. keep it short and prefer fix + revert
miguel: restarted daemonset, pods came up but still getting 504s when hitting collector. suspect TLS pinning or SNI mismatch after vendor rule
leah: flipping collector LB to accept legacy SNI for westus2 while we repair firewall rule. patch applied
miguel: after LB tweak, exporters started shipping metrics again, token ingestion rate back to normal, provisioning backlog cleared
oncall-bot: Incident noted and assigned to infra-ops, severity: Sev2, start: 1976543210
jamie: follow-up actions: 1) rollback manual firewall rule and schedule vetted maintenance window; 2) add quick e2e check in firewall runbook to verify metrics egress; 3) add exporter retry/backoff + clearer errors when TLS handshakes fail; 4) cost review for NAT usage (pri: high)
sarah: i'll create a runbook PR and a postmortem doc. will tag infra-ops and finance for the NAT cost line item
max: suggest we add exporter metric for "egress_tls_errors" so we can alert before metrics drop to 0
jamie: agreed. thanks everyone, closing thread once infra-ops confirms firewall rollback and we have runbook PR link
